checks.result: The compact connected product SU(N)^E with smooth bounded real V has compact resolvent and a strictly positive simple ground function. Gauge equivariance and simplicity force invariance. The ground-state transform cancels the potential and all mixed terms to give x/(2a) times the weighted gradient form. Smooth positive psi and psi inverse preserve H^1 on each fixed graph; no volume-uniform Sobolev equivalence is used.

checks.method: Independent proof rederivation and parameter audit
checks.result: After removing only V_hit, the conditional expectation factors into the block heat kernel and a common positive exterior weight. Since 0 <= V_hit <= 2 b p_B/x, the same-time ground-function ratio is at most exp(4 s b p_B/x^2) kappa_N(s)^m. Squaring it bounds the conditional density ratio. The minimizing-constant variance comparison costs exactly this density ratio, producing d_B(s)=x C_F/(2a) kappa_N(s)^(-2m) exp(-8 s b p_B/x^2). No exterior-volume-dependent energy or potential bound is introduced.

checks.method: Independent Casimir normalization and root-weight check
checks.result: For orthonormal fields corresponding to i t_alpha with Tr(t_alpha t_beta)=delta_alpha_beta/2, the fundamental Casimir is (N^2-1)/(2N). In the conventional root inner product with long roots squared 2, C(lambda)=(lambda,lambda+2rho)/2. The fundamental-weight pairings min(i,j)(N-max(i,j))/N are nonnegative. For any nonzero dominant integral lambda, subtracting one present fundamental weight leaves a dominant nonnegative combination, so C(lambda) is at least a fundamental Casimir. Their minimum is C_F. Product spectra add, leaving the same first nonzero eigenvalue.

The conditional density is smooth positive on the fixed compact product. Differentiating P gives conditional derivatives plus covariance with 2 grad_y log psi, hence a fixed-graph H^1 bound. Q of smooth approximants proves both form-domain core density and density in Ran Q. The restricted form is closed because Ran Q is L^2 closed. Gauge transformations act separately on selected/exterior link variables and preserve both Haar and psi, so P commutes with gauge action. The b p_B=0 case splits exactly into a free block Laplacian and exterior Hamiltonian.

checks.method: Independent Bochner, Harnack, normalization and optimization derivations
checks.result: For f=log u, w=|grad f|^2-f_t=-Delta f and F=t w, Bochner gives (Delta-d_t)F >= 2F^2/(n t)-F/t-2 grad f dot grad F. The compact maximum principle yields F<=n/2; positive time shift justifies heat-kernel initial data. Integration along a constant-speed minimizing geodesic yields the stated Harnack factor. Integrating later points for times s,2s gives max k_s <= 2^(n/2) exp(D_N^2/(4s)); integrating earlier points for s/2,s gives min k_s >= 2^(-n/2) exp(-D_N^2/(2s)). Haar probability normalization preserves the logarithmic estimate and unit mass. The resulting ratio is 2^n exp(3D_N^2/(4s)). Minimizing A/s+B s with A=3mD_N^2/2 and B=8bp_B/x^2 gives s_*=xD_N sqrt(3m/(bp_B))/4 and minimum 4D_N sqrt(3mbp_B)/x.

The exterior-volume uniformity explicitly fixes m,p_B,N,x,b,a. The model reciprocal-cost series is exactly (A/c0) exp(C sigma) sum_{r>=1}(sigma+q r)(exp(Cq)/L)^r; since sigma>0 and q>=0 it is finite exactly when rho<1. The manuscript correctly keeps this certificate and any iterated/coarse-operator application conditional; it does not claim whole-layer uniformity.

Completion of squares gives h=s+<r,Dr>, r=q+Cp, and ker H=J ker S. The G-orthogonal decomposition of p maps under J to the fine kernel decomposition. The triangle inequality and weighted scalar Cauchy-Schwarz yield dist(v,ker H)^2 <= (gamma^(-1)+d^(-1)) h[v]. J G^(-1/2) is isometric and sends ker K onto ker H, so restricting the fine Rayleigh quotient to its excited graph space proves gap H <= gap K when the latter has excitations. Multiple zero modes and K=0 are admissible and do not invalidate the lower estimate.

Bounded C makes G bounded positive and boundedly invertible. Thus k[z]=s[G^(-1/2)z] on G^(1/2) Dom s is a closed form by equivalence of form norms. The exactly specified fine domain is carried by the bounded triangular change (p,q)->(p,q+Cp) to the direct-sum form domain, so completion and the distance argument remain valid. No unchecked unbounded operator product is used, and application to the lattice Hamiltonian is explicitly conditional on these hypotheses.

For H_M, the excited 2x2 block has determinant 1 and trace M^2+2, giving the displayed smaller eigenvalue and its decay to zero. G=diag(1,1+M^2), K has positive eigenvalue 1/(1+M^2), and the harmonic certificate is 1/(M^2+2). Backward iteration of the one-step inverse-gap estimate gives exactly the stated sum. The model profile summations use sum r/L^r=L/(L-1)^2 and sum 1/L^r=1/(L-1).

checks.method: Independent finite-sector and full-Fock derivation plus exact rational arithmetic
checks.result: In the one-particle sector C1=1/2, S1=3/2, G1=5/4, K1=6/5. In the two-particle sector D2 inverse applied to B2 gives C2=(2sqrt(2)/7,-1/7), hence S2=24/7, G2=58/49, K2=84/29. Exact fractions confirm K1<K2<3 and K2 != 2K1. Since h>=I, every normalized graph vector in the n-particle sector has energy >=n; thus these are the first two positive levels. In sector n, B_n couples only to |n-1,1> with norm sqrt(n), and D_n>=n, so ||D_n^-1 B_n||<=n^-1/2. Their direct sum is bounded, and summing the nonnegative completed-sector forms gives the stated full-Fock form construction. Unequal first two excitation spacings refute one-mode quadratic oscillator closure in the retained Fock representation.

checks.method: Independent central-background and lattice-circulation derivation plus bounded finite probes
checks.result: For i<j, translating z by e_i flips U_j(z) while the other central factors cancel, giving -I plaquette holonomy; even periods ensure this remains true across the boundary. Since all perturbations lie in the sigma_3 subgroup, U_p(t)=-exp(i t (dv)_p sigma_3/2), so 1-ReTr(U_p(t))/2=1+cos(t(dv)_p/2) and the second derivative is -(dv)_p^2/4. A single-square oriented circulation has coefficients +1,+1,-1,-1, zero discrete divergence, zero sum in each component for a block containing it, and curl 4 on that square. Central adjoint transports are identity. Exact periodic side lengths 2,4,6 were checked separately; their curl-square sums were 24,20,20. These finite checks supplement the general algebra, not establish an all-volume claim.

The main text distinguishes finite-block coercivity, conditional exact multiscale comparisons, and unproved continuum obligations. No claim in the assigned vacuum/Schur material silently promotes its constants to whole-layer, infinite-volume or continuum conclusions. The evidence section appropriately limits exact arithmetic to finite certificates.
